offence_name: Driving without a valid/effective driving licence
offence_elements: Driving a motor vehicle in a public place in contravention of Section 3 (or Section 4, age restriction).
statutory_penalty: Fine up to Rs 5,000 (increased from Rs 500 by the 2019 Amendment). Penalty is prescribed under Section 181, not Section 3 itself - Section 181 is not yet a row in legal_provisions.csv.
state_compounding_amount: NOT_VERIFIED - depends on State compounding notification

offence_name: Allowing an unlicensed/unqualified person to drive
offence_elements: Owner or person in charge permits an unlicensed or disqualified person to drive.
statutory_penalty: Fine of Rs 5,000 (increased from Rs 1,000).

offence_name: Driving while disqualified from holding a licence
offence_elements: Driving, or applying for/obtaining a licence while under a disqualification order, without disclosing it.
statutory_penalty: Fine of Rs 10,000 (increased from Rs 500).

offence_name: Driving/using an unregistered motor vehicle
offence_elements: Using a motor vehicle in a public place in contravention of Section 39 (no valid registration).
statutory_penalty: Fine in the approximate range of Rs 2,000-5,000 depending on driver/owner and vehicle type; exact current bare-act figure NOT_VERIFIED (source OCR was ambiguous).
vehicle_consequence: Possible seizure in some State enforcement practice (NOT_VERIFIED)

offence_name: Over-speeding - light motor vehicle
offence_elements: Driving an LMV in excess of the speed limit fixed under Section 112.
statutory_penalty: Fine of Rs 1,000 to Rs 2,000 (increased from a flat Rs 400).
licence_consequence: Impounding of licence on second/subsequent offence

offence_name: Over-speeding - two-wheeler
offence_elements: Driving a two-wheeler in excess of the speed limit fixed under Section 112.
statutory_penalty: Treated under the same Section 183(1) bracket as light motor vehicles (Rs 1,000-2,000); a separate two-wheeler-specific figure was not confirmed in sources reviewed.
licence_consequence: Impounding of licence on second/subsequent offence

offence_name: Over-speeding - medium/heavy goods or passenger vehicle
offence_elements: Driving a medium/heavy goods or passenger vehicle in excess of the speed limit fixed under Section 112.
statutory_penalty: Fine of Rs 2,000 to Rs 4,000 (increased from a flat Rs 400).
licence_consequence: Impounding of licence on second/subsequent offence

offence_name: Racing or speed trial on a public road without authorisation
offence_elements: Driving in a race or speed trial on a public road without the written consent of the State Government/authorised authority.
statutory_penalty: Fine of Rs 5,000 (increased from Rs 500).

offence_name: Riding/driving a two-wheeler without protective headgear
offence_elements: Contravening the Section 129 requirement to wear protective headgear.
statutory_penalty: Fine of approximately Rs 1,000 with possible 3-month licence disqualification, per Section 194D - exact current figure NOT_VERIFIED against a bare-act or gazette source in this session.

offence_name: Driving/riding without wearing a seat belt
offence_elements: Contravening the Section 194B requirement to wear a seat belt.
statutory_penalty: Fine of Rs 1,000.

offence_name: Overloading (triple-riding) of a two-wheeler
offence_elements: Carrying more persons on a two-wheeler than the seating capacity permits.
statutory_penalty: Fine of Rs 2,000 (increased from Rs 100) with 3-month licence disqualification.

offence_name: Overloading a goods vehicle beyond registered capacity
offence_elements: Carrying goods beyond the gross vehicle weight/registered capacity.
statutory_penalty: Fine of Rs 20,000, plus Rs 2,000 per additional tonne of excess load (increased from Rs 2,000 + Rs 1,000/tonne).
vehicle_consequence: Vehicle may be detained until excess load is removed (common practice, NOT_VERIFIED)

offence_name: Overloading a vehicle with passengers beyond permitted capacity
offence_elements: Carrying passengers beyond the number the vehicle is permitted to carry.
statutory_penalty: Fine of Rs 1,000 per excess passenger (new provision introduced by the 2019 Amendment).
compoundable_status: NOT_VERIFIED (new provision, not confirmed against the pre-2019 Section 200 compounding list)

offence_name: Using/driving a vehicle without valid third-party insurance
offence_elements: Using a motor vehicle in a public place in contravention of Section 146 (no valid insurance policy in force).
statutory_penalty: Fine of Rs 2,000 (increased from Rs 1,000); higher figure reported for owner vs. driver in some State enforcement summaries (NOT_VERIFIED at central level).

offence_name: Driving under the influence of alcohol/drugs - first offence
offence_elements: Driving with blood alcohol exceeding 30 mg/100 ml, or incapacitated by drugs, first offence.
statutory_penalty: Imprisonment up to 6 months and/or fine of Rs 10,000 (fine increased from Rs 2,000).
compoundable_status: FALSE (not in the compoundable list reviewed)

offence_name: Driving under the influence of alcohol/drugs - repeat offence within 3 years
offence_elements: Second or subsequent drunk-driving offence within three years of a prior conviction.
statutory_penalty: Enhanced imprisonment (commonly reported up to 2 years) and/or higher fine; exact current figure NOT_VERIFIED in this session.

offence_name: Dangerous driving - first offence
offence_elements: Driving at a speed or in a manner dangerous to the public, first offence.
statutory_penalty: Imprisonment of 6 months to 1 year and/or fine of Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000.

offence_name: Dangerous driving - repeat offence within 3 years
offence_elements: Second or subsequent dangerous-driving offence within three years.
statutory_penalty: Enhanced imprisonment (commonly reported up to 2 years) and/or higher fine (commonly reported up to Rs 10,000); exact current figure NOT_VERIFIED in this session.

offence_name: Disobedience of lawful orders / refusal to provide information
offence_elements: Failing to comply with a lawful direction of, or refusing to give information to, a competent authority or police officer.
statutory_penalty: Fine of Rs 2,000 (increased from Rs 500).

offence_name: Travelling in a public service vehicle without a valid ticket
offence_elements: Travelling in, or boarding/alighting from, a stage carriage without a proper ticket.
statutory_penalty: Fine of Rs 500 (increased from Rs 200).

offence_name: Using a transport vehicle without the required permit
offence_elements: Using a transport vehicle in a public place without a valid permit under Chapter V.
statutory_penalty: Fine of up to Rs 10,000 (increased from up to Rs 5,000).
vehicle_consequence: Vehicle may be detained pending permit verification (common practice, NOT_VERIFIED)
permit_consequence: Permit may be suspended/cancelled on repeat violation

offence_name: Aggregator operating in violation of licensing conditions
offence_elements: A transport aggregator (e.g. ride-hailing platform) operates without, or in breach of, its licence conditions - a new offence category introduced by the 2019 Amendment.
statutory_penalty: Fine ranging from Rs 25,000 to Rs 1,00,000.

offence_name: Plying an oversized vehicle without authorisation
offence_elements: Operating a vehicle whose dimensions exceed prescribed limits without required authorisation - new offence introduced by the 2019 Amendment.
statutory_penalty: Fine of Rs 5,000.

offence_name: Failing to give way to an emergency vehicle
offence_elements: Failing to give way to a fire tender, ambulance or other emergency vehicle - new offence introduced by the 2019 Amendment.
statutory_penalty: Fine of Rs 10,000.

offence_name: Motor vehicle offence committed by a juvenile driver
offence_elements: A juvenile drives a motor vehicle and commits an offence; the guardian/owner is deemed guilty unless they prove the offence occurred without their knowledge or despite reasonable steps to prevent it.
statutory_penalty: Guardian/owner liable to a fine of Rs 25,000 and imprisonment (term commonly reported as up to 3 years - not independently confirmed in this session); vehicle registration liable to cancellation; juvenile dealt with under the Juvenile Justice Act and disqualified from obtaining a licence until age 25.
licence_consequence: Juvenile barred from licence until 25 (commonly reported, NOT_VERIFIED)
compoundable_status: FALSE (new, serious provision - not treated as compoundable)

offence_name: Taking or driving away a vehicle without the owners consent
offence_elements: Taking or driving away a motor vehicle without the consent of the owner or other lawful authority.
statutory_penalty: Imprisonment up to 3 months and/or fine up to Rs 500 - this figure is from a pre-2019 source; whether it was revised by the 2019 Amendment is NOT_VERIFIED.

offence_name: Contravention of the Act/rules with no specific penalty provided
offence_elements: Any contravention of the Act, rules, regulations or notifications for which no other penalty is specifically provided.
statutory_penalty: Fine up to Rs 500 for a first offence; up to Rs 1,500 for a second or subsequent offence.

offence_name: Causing death by rash/negligent driving, reported promptly
offence_elements: Causing death by rash or negligent driving, not amounting to culpable homicide, and reporting the accident to police/Magistrate soon after.
statutory_penalty: Imprisonment up to 5 years, and fine (amount not specified as a fixed figure in the Sanhita - left to court discretion).

offence_name: Causing death by rash/negligent driving, then fleeing without reporting
offence_elements: Causing death by rash or negligent driving and fleeing the scene without reporting to police/Magistrate soon after.
statutory_penalty: Imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine (amount not specified as a fixed figure in the Sanhita - left to court discretion). Commencement of this specific sub-section is unresolved as of last verification.

offence_name: Using a vehicle emitting smoke/emissions beyond prescribed limits (no valid PUC)
offence_elements: Using a motor vehicle without a valid Pollution Under Control certificate, or emitting smoke/vapour beyond prescribed limits.
statutory_penalty: Commonly reported as a fine in the range of Rs 1,000 (first offence) to Rs 2,000 (subsequent offence); exact current bare-act/rule figure NOT_VERIFIED in this session.
